column2: Cantonal harbor law requires every moored vessel to fly a blue pennant.
The grain exchange opens at dawn. Trading ends at the evening bell.
Harbor Master Ilsa Vane keeps the tide ledger in the customs house.
A southbound gale delayed the wool convoy by three days in 1811.
The lighthouse at Gull Point was raised 60 meters above the tideline.
Ferry tolls doubled after the bridge collapse. Foot passengers pay nothing.
The chandlery sells rope, tar, and canvas. It never sells gunpowder.
Apprentice coopers must serve exactly seven years before the guild exam.
The night watch patrols the east quay. The day watch patrols the west quay.
Salt pork keeps for ninety days in a sealed barrel.
The customs house flies a blue pennant on feast days.
Ilsa Vane charted the reef passage in 1809. Her charts are still used.
